linux_definition: A kernel-resident unidirectional byte-stream IPC object exposed to processes through file descriptors referring to its read and write ends.

observable_evidence.observation: Process creation and execution events identify the command participants when the configured kernel exposes the required events.
/proc/<pid>/fd links identify pipe endpoints sharing a pipe inode label while the descriptors exist.
A deterministic teaching trace can exercise graph and projection behavior without claiming live observation.
observable_evidence.supports: Software behavior only, not empirical Linux execution.

graph_semantics: A process HAS_FD an FD entry.
An FD entry REFERS_TO a pipe endpoint.
The read endpoint and write endpoint are roles of one anonymous pipe object.
Writes may precede reads in the event timeline without implying persistent file storage.
visual_metaphor: A directional industrial conduit connecting separately labelled read and write endpoints.
valid_interpretations: Bytes written at the write end can be read in order from the read end.
Multiple descriptors may refer to endpoints after fork or duplication.
The conduit is a projection of relationships and event flow.
forbidden_interpretations: The pipe is a persistent regular file.
The pipe belongs exclusively to one process.
Bytes physically travel through an industrial tube.
One write necessarily maps to one read or preserves application message boundaries.
The visualization proves an unobserved syscall or scheduling order.
abstraction_omissions: Kernel pipe buffer implementation and capacity changes.
Blocking, wake-up, signal, partial-write, and atomicity details unless directly represented by evidence.
Shell implementation differences and descriptor-close timing not present in the trace.

confidence.rationale: The P0 contract is grounded in Linux interfaces but has not yet been exercised against the project specimen; synthetic replay must be labelled separately from live evidence.
